extraction.name: VideoChat-Flash: Hierarchical Compression for Long-Context Video Modeling
extraction.description: VideoChat-Flash is a multimodal large language model (MLLM) for long-context video modeling. It introduces a Hierarchical video token Compression (HiCo) method, a large-scale dataset named LongVid, a multi-stage short-to-long learning scheme, and a challenging 'Multi-Hop Needle-In-A-Video-Haystack' benchmark.
extraction.creator: Xinhao Li, Yi Wang, Jiashuo Yu, Xiangyu Zeng, Yuhan Zhu, Haian Huang, Jianfei Gao, Kunchang Li, Yinan He, Chenting Wang, Yu Qiao, Yali Wang, Limin Wang
extraction.citeAs: Li, X., Wang, Y., Yu, J., Zeng, X., Zhu, Y., Huang, H., Gao, J., Li, K., He, Y., Wang, C., Qiao, Y., Wang, Y., & Wang, L. (2025). VideoChat-Flash: Hierarchical Compression for Long-Context Video Modeling. arXiv:2501.00574v4.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The LongVid dataset was constructed by leveraging existing datasets (Ego4D, HowTo100M, HDVila, MiraData). Data curation involved generating dense event labels for long videos using existing high-quality short video captions or extracting major events from captions using an LLM. QA pairs were constructed based on video captions, event labels, and timestamps.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The LongVid dataset comprises 114,228 long videos and 3,444,849 question-answering (QA) pairs. It is curated from Ego4D, HowTo100M, HD-VILA, and MiraData. Additional training data includes image-text pairs from LCS-558K, short video-text pairs from S-MiT, WebVid2M, Kinetics, COCO118K, BLIP558K, CC3M, Evo-Instruct, VideoChat2, IntemVideo2, ShareGPT4-o, VideoChatGPT-Plus, LLaV A-Video-178K, LLava-Hound, MoiveChat, and Vript.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Videos were segmented into clips. Clip-level compression was performed using spatio-temporal attention and similar token merging. Video-level compression was performed during LLM processing using progressive visual dropout (uniform drop in shallow layers, text-guided select in deep layers). Duration-based sampling was applied to videos.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Videos were sampled based on duration (dense for short, sparse for long). Frames were encoded into tokens. Tokens were compressed at the clip level (16 tokens per frame) and potentially at the video level during inference. Timestamps were added as prompts.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Event labels were generated using existing high-quality short video captions (e.g., Ego4D-HCap, HT-Step) or extracted from captions using an LLM (Qwen-72b). QA pairs were constructed based on video captions, event labels, and timestamps. Some captions were refined using AI models (VideoChat2, Gemini, LLaVA-NeXT-34B).
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The model aims to enable MLLMs to process hours-long movies, documentaries, and online video streams efficiently. It addresses the challenge of understanding extremely long video contexts while maintaining performance and reducing computational costs.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The model's performance on short videos might slightly decline when maximizing long video understanding (e.g., when Tmax reaches 512). The compression methods may lead to loss of detailed information, although HiCo aims to minimize this. The evaluation benchmark 'Multi-Hop Needle-In-A-Video-Haystack' is designed to be more challenging but may still have limitations in assessing all aspects of reasoning.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation, Fine Tuning. The dataset and model are intended for long video understanding, video QA, temporal grounding, video captioning, event relation recognition, scene relation recognition, and video event counting.
